entities.summary:
The Hong Kong flu, a global pandemic, ravaged the world between 1968 and 1970, claiming millions of lives and transforming the global healthcare landscape. 


This devastating outbreak, caused by the H3N2 subtype of the influenza A virus, spread rapidly across the globe, infecting an estimated 1 billion people and killing approximately 1-4 million, mostly the young and the elderly. 


The pandemic, which originated in Hong Kong in July 1968, spread to become one of the deadliest in modern history, with its impact felt in every corner of the world. 


The legacy of the Hong Kong flu can be seen in the increased focus on global health cooperation and the development of more effective vaccine production methods, particularly the use of egg-based vaccine production, which replaced the previous method of production in chicken embryos. 


The pandemic's impact on global healthcare was further underscored by the World Health Organization's (WHO) creation of the Global Outbreak Alert and Response Network (GOARN) in 2000, which aimed to improve global preparedness and response to infectious disease outbreaks.
